newsitem.title: USA: Icahn-led Marvel bondholders file reorganization plan. [CORRECTED 21:39 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Icahn-led Marvel bondholders file reorganization plan. [CORRECTED 21:39 GMT]

text.p: Bondholders of Marvel Entertainment Group Inc., led by investor Carl Icahn, launched a counter-attack Tuesday to scuttle a day-old bankruptcy reorganization plan devised by the comic book publisher and Toy Biz Inc.

The bondholder group said it filed its own reorganization plan in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware, which includes a $365 million rights offering. The plan also proposed the creation of a transition team to resuscitate the company, which would be led by former Marvel executive Joseph Calamari, according to the bondholders.

The filing comes one day after financier Ronald Perelman and Marvel's bankers including Chase Manhattan reached a deal to sell Marvel's comic book and entertainment operations to Toy Biz , which is controlled by Isaac Perlmutter.
Toy Biz holds the licenses to some of Marvel's characters such as Spiderman and the Hulk.

Earlier in April, Perlmutter, who owns 35 percent of Toy Biz, presented Marvel's bank lenders with an offer to buy the comic book company. The Marvel deal would flip the tables somewhat, because Marvel owns over 26 percent of Toy Biz.
Under the Marvel plan, its Fleer/SkyBox and Panini subsidiaries would be spun off to the creditor banks, and according to a source close to Toy Biz, would likely be sold.
The latest plan from the dissenting bondholders is essentially the same plan they filed in March. A bankruptcy court judge granted a temporary restraining order blocking that plan.
The company and its bondholders are to go to federal appellate court Thursday where the bondholders are seeking to lift the restraining order.

The bondholders said that Marvel's exclusivity period to file its plan of reorganization had expired as of midnight Monday. A source close to the bondholders said that as a result, the bondholders now have exclusivity rights.
Officials from Marvel were not immediately available to comment.
Marvel filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in December.
The bondholders hold about 80 percent of Marvel, because their nearly $900 million in debt is backed by Marvel equity.

Under Marvel's plan proposed Monday, the banks (corrects from bondholders) would hold about 28 percent of the company and get 100 percent of Marvel's Fleer/Sky Box trading cards business and 100 percent of its Panini sticker businesses.
Toy Biz shareholders would own the other 72 percent of Marvel, under the Marvel plan, which both the company's bondholders and some shareholders said they opposed.
The bondholders said Monday that $100 million of the $365 million rights offering would be used to retire Marvel's debtor-in-possession credit facility and to repay bondholders.
The balance of the funds, they said, would be used as working capital to restore the company to financial health.
In a separate statement Tuesday, a Philadelphia-based committee representing Marvel stockholders said it opposed the company's reorganization plan.
The committee said it had repeatedly attempted to consult with Marvel regarding the plan but Marvel had refused to discuss any proposed reorganization plan with the committee.
The committee said it could not support the new plan and would explore all available alternatives.
Stock of Marvel Entertainment fell 12.5 cents to close at $2.25 and Toy Biz was down 25 cents at $10, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
